question: Which ruler was the founder of the Nanda Dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahapadma Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mahapadma Nanda** was the founder of the **Nanda Dynasty**, which ruled over Magadha in ancient India during the 4th century BCE.
 
• He is often referred to as the "first historical emperor of India," as he established a large and powerful empire that laid the groundwork for the later Mauryan Empire.
 
• Mahapadma Nanda is considered the first ruler in Indian history to establish a **centralized empire**, uniting various regions under one rule.
 
• He belonged to a family of low caste origin, and his rise marked a significant social transformation, as he overthrew the ruling Shishunaga dynasty to ascend to power.
 
• His reign is characterized by a strong central administration and a large standing army, which made the Nanda Dynasty an influential power in ancient India.
